lines.name: Architect Server licences
lines.recognitionNote: Right to use: revenue at one point in time, when the keys are delivered and the customer can use the software.

lines.name: Insight Cloud subscription
lines.recognitionNote: Right to access (SaaS): revenue evenly over the 36 months.

lines.name: Insight Cloud overage
lines.recognitionNote: Variable consideration: recognised in the month the extra users are there, at the contract rate.

lines.name: Flow Engine consumption
lines.model: Software on consumption, billed in arrears
lines.recognitionNote: Usage-based fee: revenue as the calls are made. Not part of the committed price.

lines.name: Implementation
lines.recognitionNote: Over time by progress (hours worked against plan). Billing follows the milestones, so the two differ.

lines.name: Training
lines.recognitionNote: Recognised when a training day has been held; billed at the end of that month.

lines.name: Managed operations (Premium)
lines.recognitionNote: Stand-ready service: revenue evenly over the 36 months.

title: Revenue Recognition (Software)

steps.name: Identify the contract
steps.question: Is there an enforceable contract, and are these papers one contract or several?
steps.case: Contract C-4410 (signed 2026-10-28) with Kestrel Versicherung AG: rights and payment terms are clear, the customer has the commitment, payment is probable. The order form, the master agreement and the service description are read as one contract because they were negotiated together.
steps.judge: Combining contracts signed at about the same time; contract term when either side can cancel; free pilots before the contract; side letters.

steps.name: Identify the performance obligations
steps.question: Which promises are distinct, so that each gets its own revenue?
steps.case: Five committed obligations: Architect Server licences, Insight Cloud subscription, implementation, training, managed operations. Overage and consumption are not promised in advance; they are usage that adds up later.
steps.judge: Is the implementation distinct from the cloud service, or does it change the service so much that both are one obligation? Is support part of the licence or separate?

steps.name: Determine the transaction price
steps.question: What does the company expect to receive?
steps.case: Fixed 388,000.00 EUR. On top: overage at 34.00 per extra user and 0.40 per 1,000 API calls. These are variable and are not in the fixed price. Possible reductions: service credits for missed availability, volume rebate.
steps.judge: Variable consideration (estimate, then limit it so a large reversal is not likely), service credits, rebates, significant financing (payment terms beyond one year), money paid to the customer.

steps.name: Allocate the price
steps.question: How is the price shared out to the obligations?
steps.case: By stand-alone selling price: 416,700.00 at list, 388,000.00 charged, so a discount of 28,700.00 (6.9 %) is shared proportionally. Usage and overage stay out because their rates match the stand-alone price.
steps.judge: Evidence for the stand-alone price (what do others pay for the same?); relative method or residual approach; whether the discount belongs to one obligation only.

steps.name: Recognise the revenue
steps.question: When is each obligation satisfied?
steps.case: Licences at one point in time when the keys are delivered (2026-11-04). Subscription and managed operations evenly over 36 months from 2026-12-01. Implementation by progress, training by day held, usage and overage as they arise.
steps.judge: Licence or service? Point in time or over time? Method for measuring progress. Customer acceptance clauses.

treatments.name: Perpetual on-premise licence
treatments.why: The customer can run the software on its own systems. It is a right to use the software as it exists. Revenue when the keys are delivered and the licence period has started.
treatments.watch: A customer acceptance clause can delay the point. Updates that are promised are a separate service.

treatments.name: Term licence on-premise (for example 3 years)
treatments.why: The licence part is recognised at the start of the term, not spread over it. Support for the term is a separate service, recognised evenly.
treatments.watch: Multi-year payment in arrears can contain a financing component. A renewal is recognised at the start of the renewal period, never earlier.
treatments.je: Dr Receivable, Cr Revenue (licence); Dr Receivable, Cr Deferred revenue (support)

treatments.name: Software as a service (subscription)
treatments.why: The customer gets access, not the software. The company stands ready every day, so revenue is spread evenly over the term.
treatments.watch: If the customer can take the software and run it elsewhere without a major penalty, it is a licence plus hosting instead.
treatments.je: Dr Receivable, Cr Deferred revenue; each month Dr Deferred revenue, Cr Revenue

treatments.name: Hosted licence (customer could take possession)
treatments.why: Two parts: the licence at one point in time, the hosting evenly over the term.
treatments.watch: Needs an honest answer to: could the customer run it on its own or a third party's hardware without a significant penalty?
treatments.je: Split the price by stand-alone price first

treatments.name: Support and maintenance
treatments.why: A ready-to-help promise, recognised evenly. Updates that come when and if available are part of it.
treatments.watch: If the support is so basic that the customer needs it to use the software, it can be one obligation with the licence.
treatments.je: Dr Receivable, Cr Deferred revenue; monthly release to Revenue

treatments.name: Consumption fee (per call, per transaction)
treatments.why: The amount depends on use. It is recognised in the month the use happens, at the contract rate.
treatments.watch: Two rules look similar: for a licence of intellectual property the royalty is recognised at the later of use and satisfaction; for a service the fee belongs to the period of use. Check the rate against the stand-alone price.
treatments.je: Dr Contract asset (or Receivable), Cr Revenue each month; invoice later

treatments.name: Overage above a committed volume
treatments.why: The extra users or calls are variable. Revenue in the month they occur, invoiced in arrears.
treatments.watch: If the overage rate is far below the normal price, part of the committed price may have to move to it.
treatments.je: Dr Contract asset, Cr Revenue; on invoice Dr Receivable, Cr Contract asset

treatments.name: Implementation and configuration
treatments.why: If another company could do it and the cloud service works without it, it is distinct: revenue by hours worked against plan or by milestones that show real progress.
treatments.watch: If the work changes the service itself, it is one obligation with the subscription and follows its pattern.
treatments.je: Invoice by milestone: Dr Receivable, Cr Deferred revenue; progress: Dr Deferred revenue or Contract asset, Cr Revenue

treatments.name: Training
treatments.why: Each day held is revenue. Prepaid vouchers are deferred and released when used or when the customer will not use them.
treatments.watch: Unused vouchers (breakage) need an estimate based on history.
treatments.je: Dr Receivable, Cr Deferred revenue; Dr Deferred revenue, Cr Revenue per day

treatments.name: Managed operations
treatments.why: A stand-ready service, recognised evenly over the term.
treatments.watch: Penalties for missed service levels reduce the price.
treatments.je: Dr Receivable, Cr Deferred revenue; monthly release

treatments.name: Free trial or pilot
treatments.why: Without a payment or a binding commitment there is no contract yet, so nothing is recognised.
treatments.watch: A discount on the later purchase can be a material right.

treatments.name: Renewal option at a discount
treatments.why: If the discount is larger than what other customers get, the option is a material right: part of today's price is deferred until the renewal or the option expires.
treatments.watch: Estimate the likelihood that the customer renews.
treatments.je: Part of the price goes to Deferred revenue

treatments.name: Sale through a reseller
treatments.why: If the reseller is the customer, revenue when control passes to the reseller. If the reseller only arranges the sale, the company recognises on sale to the end customer.
treatments.watch: Right of return, price protection and sell-through reporting.
treatments.je: Depends on who controls the software

treatments.name: Payment terms beyond one year
treatments.why: A significant financing component splits the price into revenue and interest income. Within a year the practical expedient says: ignore it.
treatments.watch: Multi-year licences paid at the end are the typical case.
treatments.je: Dr Receivable, Cr Revenue and Cr Interest income over time

scenarios.name: Add 50 users from April 2027
scenarios.text: The customer adds 50 users to Insight Cloud for the rest of the term, at 28.00 per user and month. The stand-alone price is 30.00.

scenarios.name: Add 10 licences and 50 users, deep discount
scenarios.text: One amendment adds 10 Architect Server licences (1,200.00 each, stand-alone price 1,600.00) and 50 users at 20.00 per month (stand-alone price 30.00).

commission.note: Incremental cost of obtaining the contract: capitalised and amortised over the expected customer life of five years, because renewals are expected and the commission on renewals is lower.

judgements.question: Can the customer use the implementation without the cloud service, and could someone else do it?
judgements.risk: Revenue for implementation is shown too early if it is really part of the service.
judgements.control: Written assessment per contract type, approved once and reviewed for new offers

judgements.question: What do we actually charge for each piece when sold alone?
judgements.risk: A list price that nobody pays moves revenue between obligations.
judgements.control: Yearly SSP study with ranges; deals outside the range are flagged

judgements.question: Can the customer take the software and run it elsewhere?
judgements.risk: Licence revenue up front when it should be spread.
judgements.control: Checklist in the deal review, evidence in the contract file

judgements.question: How much of overage, rebates and credits is likely to stay?
judgements.risk: Revenue reversed in a later quarter.
judgements.control: Estimate each quarter, compare with actual, keep the constraint note

judgements.question: Can the customer leave early without a real penalty?
judgements.control: Legal flags termination for convenience; term set accordingly

judgements.question: Does the company control what the end customer receives?
judgements.control: Decision memo for marketplaces and resellers

judgements.question: Does the customer have a right to reject?
judgements.risk: Revenue before the customer has accepted.
judgements.control: Acceptance date is a posting condition

judgements.question: Did sales promise anything outside the contract?
judgements.risk: Unrecorded rights to returns, free periods or future products.

judgements.question: Is an upsell a separate contract or a change of this one?
judgements.risk: Wrong pattern for the added users.
judgements.control: Decision tree in the process; reviewed above a value limit

judgements.question: Is payment more than a year after delivery?
judgements.control: Payment terms flagged at order entry

judgements.question: Was the keys delivery really before the quarter end?
judgements.risk: Licence revenue booked in the wrong quarter.
judgements.control: Key issue date from the entitlement system is the evidence

judgements.question: Which commissions are incremental, and how long do they last?
judgements.risk: Costs expensed too early or kept too long.
judgements.control: Commission plan mapped to the policy; yearly impairment check
